# The provisional vessel chrome's replacement branch bypasses its own retire guard

## Context

Ada's review of PR #19212 (approved, review 5317488350) left three optional notes. The polish for notes 1 and 3 was committed as 90174829da on the PR's branch three minutes after the operator merged it at def5b265ab, so it never reached `dev`. This leaf lands it.

## The Problem

`VesselWorkspace#resolveVesselStageTarget` replaces a chrome that lost its viewport (destroyed, or re-homed) with `chrome?.isDestroyed || chrome?.destroy()`. That branch destroys a live-but-detached chrome without the body check `retireProvisionalVesselChrome` enforces: if the chrome still held the staged pane, the live pane would be destroyed with it — the invariant the PR's own docblock states never happens. No flow reaches it today (a destroyed viewport destroys its children first), so this is a latent contradiction between two paths, not a live defect. The same methods also guard shapes the class guarantees (`getCardContainer?.()`, `items?.length`), which reads as uncertainty about the chrome's own type.

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs`: `resolveVesselStageTarget(windowId)` creates one `Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.TabContainer` per vessel window as the tear-out embodiment's stage target; `retireProvisionalVesselChrome(windowId, {releasePanes})` is the one place that knows how to end it — refusing while the body holds a pane unless the caller takes the pane over, then removing and destroying.
- A tab container's `items` are its bar and its body; the staged pane lives in `getCardContainer().items`.

## The Fix

1. The replacement branch calls `retireProvisionalVesselChrome(windowId, {releasePanes: true})` instead of destroying directly, so a chrome that lost its viewport hands any pane it still holds over detached and retires through the same guard.
2. `getCardContainer()` and `items.length` are called plainly; the one remaining optional chain guards a real `null` (no body once the chrome is gone).
3. A unit arm pins the replacement: a chrome removed from its viewport while holding the staged pane is replaced on the next resolve, the pane survives detached, and the old chrome is destroyed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 `Workspace.spec.mjs` carries the replacement arm (the pane survives, the old chrome is destroyed, a new chrome sits in the viewport), red on `dev`, green at the PR head; the whole spec green.
- [ ] AC-2 The diff removes the direct `destroy()` from the replacement branch and the class-shape optional chains; no behaviour of the stage, mount or retirement paths changes (the five-beat morph arms stay green headless).

## Out of Scope

Note 2 of the same review (the resolver creates before the engine's `stage` validates): kept as the seam's design, see the PR's disposition comment.
